To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lens plasma membrane is capable of regulating the cytoplasmic calcium concentration in lens fibers by the action of a calmodulin-dependent calcium pump and a Na/Ca exchanger.
plasma-membrane vesicles derived from lens fiber cells possess an ATP-dependent calcium pump, which is regulated by calmodulin, and which is inhibited by vanadate.
The lens plasma membrane contains a Ca2+ ATPase that is regulated by cAMP-dependent protein kinases, and that the Ca2+ ATPases are inhibited by vanadate and R24571, and stimulated by valinomycin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of Ca2+ regulation in lens fiber cell plasma membranes.
the regulation of cytosolic Ca(2+) concentration in lens cells.
the regulation of calcium by lens fiber cells, and the possible role of calcium in lens fiber cell cataract formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
calcium regulation by lens fiber cell cytoplasm is mediated by both the calcium pump and a Na:Ca exchanger.
lens plasma membranes are capable of regulating cytosolic Ca concentration by several processes.
the lens plasma membrane is involved in the regulation of fiber cell cytosol [Ca2+].
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lens is a good model to study calcium homeostasis.

the lens is capable of maintaining a very low cytosolic Ca concentration, but is also capable of releasing large amounts of Ca when the need arises, and that this ability may be lost with the aging lens.
the regulation of cytosolic calcium concentration is a dynamic process that is mediated by the plasma membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plasma membrane of lens fibers contains a calcium pump, which is inhibited by oxidation of -SH groups, and that this calcium pump is likely regulated by calmodulin.
the lens fiber cell plasma membrane has a number of calcium transporters that could be involved in the regulation of cytosolic calcium concentration.
